title: Is a Pakistan-US trade deal close?
credits: Photos: Shujaat Muzaffar, Muhammad Amir / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: Pakistan and the United States say they are close to a new trade agreement.
Commerce Secretary Jawad Paul says both sides have made substantial progress on a bilateral reciprocal trade deal.
He says only a few technical points remain, to be settled with the office of the US Trade Representative.
He made the remarks at a meeting between Commerce Minister Jam Kamal Khan and the US charge d'affaires, Natalie Baker.
Pakistan wants faster US inspection visits, so that Pakistani mangoes can be exported to America.
It is also pushing for market access for Pakistani dates, which would help growers, especially in Balochistan.
The US side wants to sell more cotton and soybeans to Pakistan.
Both sides also discussed American investment in farm machinery, food processing, cold storage, and minerals and mining.
Pakistan raised concerns about disrupted land trade routes with Afghanistan and Central Asia.
Karachi will host the FoodAg twenty twenty-six exhibition from the twenty-third to the twenty-sixth of November.
A deal could open new doors for Pakistani exporters in one of the world's biggest markets.
